title: NFPA 101 Testing: Monthly 30-Second & Annual 90-Minute Tests

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Office corridor with emergency units and exit signs; tech and building engineer with a clipboard and a remote test wand. Presenter voice-over.
scenes.says: Job mindset. A breaker-off test darkens the space, and operating breakers puts you at an open panel. Warn occupants, keep people off ladders and stairs, carry a flashlight, and follow our NFPA 70E procedures. Plan before you go: the unit list or floor plan, ladders, a test wand for high units, switch keys, and a schedule the customer agreed to.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Matthew in the corridor, medium close-up.
scenes.on_screen: Scope varies by state and city. The AHJ may require its own forms or inspectors.
scenes.says: Scope varies by state and city. In some areas a lighting tech may test emergency lighting and keep the records under the company's license. In others it must be done by, or under the supervision of, a licensed electrician, and some jobs need a permit and inspection. The AHJ may also require specific inspectors or its own forms. Confirm with your supervisor first.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.on_screen: Monthly: at least 30 seconds | Annual: full 90 minutes | Record every test
scenes.says: Why test? Batteries age, lamps fail, chargers die, and people wire units to switched legs. NFPA 101 requires a functional test every 30 days for at least 30 seconds, and an annual test for the full 1.5 hours, 90 minutes. Every test gets a written record for the AHJ. Units must work for the full duration, and failures get repaired and documented.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Monthly walk: tech checks charge light, presses and holds a test switch; uses a remote test wand on a high unit; checks an exit sign's letters and chevrons; engineer logs on a tablet.
scenes.on_screen: 1 Charge light on  2 Hold test 30+ s  3 Steady light  4 Back to charging  5 Exit sign check  6 Aim  7 Record
scenes.says: Monthly, each unit. Confirm the charge indicator is lit. Press and hold the test switch, or use the remote, for at least 30 seconds. Lamps come on promptly and stay steady. Release, and it goes back to charging. Exit signs: EXIT fully lit and legible, chevrons correct, faces undamaged, not blocked. Heads aimed down the egress path. Record it.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Close-up: self-testing unit's status LED with indicator code chart.
scenes.on_screen: Self-testing units: still check indicators and keep records
scenes.says: Self-testing units run the 30-second test automatically at least every 30 days and show failures on a status light. They still need a periodic visual check of the indicators and records, and the annual test requirement still applies, though they may run it automatically. Learn each unit's indicator codes. Generator and central inverter systems are usually tested with facilities staff or a specialty vendor.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Annual test: tech gets the manager's OK, posts a sign, a qualified person turns off the lighting breakers; tech writes the start time.
scenes.on_screen: Annual: confirm full charge | start | record start time | check at 90 min
scenes.says: Annual test. Make sure units have had their full charge time, new ones often 24 hours. Get permission and schedule it so the building isn't occupied, or test a portion at a time so not every unit is discharged at once. Start the test, by breaker or a timed test function, and record the start time. Check partway through to catch early failures.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: At the 90-minute mark, tech walks the floor; one unit is dark. Breakers restored, charge lights come on.
scenes.on_screen: Dark, dim or off before 90 minutes = FAIL
scenes.says: At the end of 90 minutes, check every unit. A unit that goes dark, dims badly or shuts off before 90 minutes fails, even if it lit for an hour. Restore normal power, confirm every unit is charging, and record each result, the duration and the restore time. Remind the customer that recharging can take up to 24 hours, so emergency capacity is reduced until then.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Close-up of a log entry: date/time, unit ID and location, test type, result, corrective action, initials.
scenes.on_screen: Date/time | Unit ID & location | Test type | Result | Corrective action | Tester
scenes.says: A complete record has the date and time, unit ID and location, test type, pass or fail with a description, corrective action, and the tester's name or initials. Software or self-diagnostic logs are fine, as long as records are kept and available to the AHJ. And never leave a breaker off at the end without the customer knowing.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Matthew in the corridor, medium shot.
scenes.on_screen: Now read the lesson and take the quiz.
scenes.says: Thirty seconds monthly, ninety minutes yearly, every unit checked at the end, and every test written down. Now read the lesson and take the quiz.
